subsystems.name: Environment model
subsystems.role: represents the target network: hosts, services, vulnerabilities and connections.

subsystems.name: Agent or planner
subsystems.role: decides the next action — scan, exploit, pivot, escalate — to reach a goal.
parts: policy network (reinforcement learning) or language model

subsystems.name: Action execution layer
subsystems.role: carries out chosen actions using real security tools.
parts: remote access and lateral movement tools

subsystems.name: Observation and state updater
subsystems.role: collects results from actions and updates the environment model.

subsystems.name: Safe execution sandbox
subsystems.role: keeps the agent contained so it cannot damage real systems.

subsystems.name: Reporting and remediation
subsystems.role: turns discovered attack paths into findings for defenders.

buildSteps.title: Build a target environment
buildSteps.detail: Create a realistic network — either a digital twin of the real one or a cyber range — with hosts, services, users and known weaknesses.

buildSteps.title: Define the agent interface
buildSteps.detail: Specify the observation space (what the agent sees) and action space (what it can try), using tactics from frameworks such as MITRE ATT&CK.

buildSteps.title: Generate or collect experience
buildSteps.detail: Run human red-team playbooks, scripted attacks, or millions of simulated episodes to give the agent examples of successful and failed paths.

buildSteps.title: Train the decision maker
buildSteps.detail: Use reinforcement learning with rewards for reaching goals and penalties for noise, or fine-tune a language model to reason over tool outputs and pick actions.

buildSteps.title: Validate against a baseline
buildSteps.detail: Compare the agent's findings, speed and false-positive rate with a human red team on the same range.

buildSteps.title: Connect to real tools under guardrails
buildSteps.detail: Integrate scanners and exploitation frameworks, but enforce scope limits, human approval for risky actions, and full logging.

buildSteps.title: Deploy for continuous testing
buildSteps.detail: Run the agent on a schedule against production-like environments, feeding results to defenders and retraining as the network changes.

prerequisites.why: they let an agent learn sequences of actions toward a distant goal.

prerequisites.tech: Mature offensive security tooling with APIs
prerequisites.why: scanners, exploitation frameworks and remote access tools are the agent's hands.

prerequisites.tech: Realistic network simulation and cyber ranges
prerequisites.why: training and safe testing require environments that behave like real enterprise networks.

prerequisites.tech: Large language models for tool use
prerequisites.why: they help interpret unstructured outputs and plan, but can hallucinate or take unsafe actions.
an autonomous attacker must be impossible to leak beyond its authorised scope.

pathway.milestone: automated scanners and scripted exploitation in lab environments
pathway.unlocks: faster, repeatable discovery of known vulnerabilities.

pathway.milestone: agents that chain multiple exploits and move laterally in cyber ranges
pathway.unlocks: testing of defence-in-depth against realistic multi-step attacks.

pathway.milestone: hybrid teams where a human red-teamer directs several AI agents
pathway.unlocks: scaled continuous testing without losing human judgement.

pathway.milestone: fully autonomous red teaming inside strict guardrails
pathway.unlocks: round-the-clock adversarial testing of live networks — if safety and control problems are solved.
